patients.summary: Thirty-year-old marketing coordinator with generalized anxiety disorder, hypothyroidism and iron deficiency anemia who joined in August 2024 while planning a pregnancy. Her first pregnancy ended with PPROM at 35 weeks complicated by chorioamnionitis and a preterm vaginal birth in May 2025; her second ended with a term vaginal birth in May 2026. Primary care follows her mood, thyroid and iron between two obstetric courses.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27F here to get set up with us. Had been seeing a PCP in the area but wanted a practice she can reach directly. Records release signed today.

She would like to start trying for a pregnancy this fall, which is why she has been on a prenatal vitamin with iron for a few months. Wants to make sure her thyroid and anxiety are where they should be before then.

Anxiety: GAD, on sertraline 50 for some time, feels it works. Some worry around work deadlines, sleeps fine. No panic attacks. Not interested in changing anything. GAD-7 6, PHQ-9 3.
Thyroid: hypothyroid, levothyroxine 88 mcg each morning, takes it apart from the vitamin. Last TSH was "normal" per her, will see records.
Iron: told years ago she was iron deficient. Gets her iron from the prenatal now. Uses docusate now and then for constipation from the iron.

PSH: lap appendectomy at 16; wisdom teeth out.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg daily; sertraline 50 mg daily; prenatal vitamin w/ iron 1 tab daily; docusate 100 mg prn.
Allergies: PENICILLIN - anaphylaxis. LATEX - contact dermatitis (gloves).
FH: mother had preterm premature rupture of membranes with a pregnancy. Father with type 2 diabetes. Sister had chorioamnionitis in a prior pregnancy.
SH: marketing coordinator. Never smoked. No alcohol at all right now. Never pregnant.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing, pleasant. Thyroid smooth, not enlarged, no nodules. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, well-healed laparoscopic scars. No edema. Affect bright, speech normal.

A/P
1. GAD - stable on sertraline 50. Talked through sertraline in pregnancy; reasonable to continue, she prefers to stay on it.
2. Hypothyroidism - TSH today. Once pregnant she should let us know right away so we can recheck.
3. Iron deficiency anemia - CBC and ferritin. Continue prenatal with iron.
4. Preconception - on prenatal vitamin already. CMP for baseline.
5. Health maintenance - will look for her last Pap in outside records. Flu/COVID this fall.

Follow up after labs, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Iris, your labs from yesterday are in. Thyroid level is normal on the 88 mcg, so no change. Kidney, liver and sugar are normal. Your hemoglobin is 11.9, just under the normal range, and your ferritin (iron stores) is 16, on the low side. That fits with the iron deficiency you've had before. Keep taking the prenatal with iron every day, and we will recheck in a few months or once you are pregnant. Let me know if you have questions.

documents.title: Positive test!
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I took a test this morning and it was positive! First day of my last period was August 27. You said to let you know right away for the thyroid. Also is it really ok to keep taking the sertraline? I'm a little nervous now that it's real. Who should I see for OB?

documents.title: RE: Positive test!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Congratulations! That puts you at about 5 weeks. I've put in a referral to an obstetrics group near you; they usually see new pregnancies around 8 weeks. I also ordered a thyroid level (TSH and free T4), you can come in for the blood draw any morning this week or next.

Yes, keep taking the sertraline 50 mg. It is one of the most studied medicines in pregnancy, and stopping it suddenly would be the bigger risk for you. Keep the levothyroxine and prenatal vitamin going too. Any bleeding or bad cramping, call us or the OB right away.

documents.title: Obstetrics Consultation Letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Thank you for referring Ms. Castro, whom we saw on 10/24/2024 for her initial obstetric visit. She is a 28-year-old G1P0 at 8 weeks 2 days by a certain last menstrual period of 8/27/2024.

History reviewed: generalized anxiety disorder on sertraline 50 mg, hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 88 mcg, history of iron deficiency anemia on a prenatal vitamin with iron. Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), latex. Family history notable for PPROM in her mother and chorioamnionitis in her sister.

Transvaginal ultrasound showed a single intrauterine pregnancy with cardiac activity, crown-rump length consistent with dates. EDD 6/3/2025 by LMP, confirmed by ultrasound.

Initial prenatal labs: HIV nonreactive, hepatitis B surface antigen negative, hepatitis C antibody nonreactive, RPR nonreactive. Remaining routine prenatal labs were unremarkable.

Plan: continue current medications. We will follow her through the pregnancy and send updates. Please continue to manage her thyroid and anxiety; we would appreciate copies of TSH results.

Sincerely,
Obstetrics

S: 20 wks today, G1. Followed by OB, everything has been routine so far, anatomy scan scheduled next week. Anxiety a bit up with the pregnancy, mostly worry about whether things are going ok between appointments. Still sleeping. No panic. Taking sertraline 50 daily, levothyroxine 88 in the morning, prenatal w/ iron, docusate sometimes. No palpitations, no heat or cold intolerance.
GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 4.

O: vitals as charted, weight up as expected. Comfortable. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Gravid abdomen. No edema. Mood a little anxious, affect full.

A/P:
1. GAD - mild uptick, reasonable for circumstances. Discussed options; she'd rather not change the dose. Gave info on perinatal counseling resources if she wants them. Continue sertraline 50.
2. Hypothyroidism - TSH/FT4 today, will forward to OB.
3. IDA - OB is following her CBC in pregnancy. Continue prenatal with iron.
RTC after delivery or sooner.

Indication: suspected rupture of membranes at 35 weeks 2 days.
Single live intrauterine pregnancy. Cephalic presentation. Fetal cardiac activity present.
Amniotic fluid index: 3 cm.
Biophysical profile: fetal breathing 2/2, gross body movement 2/2, fetal tone 2/2, amniotic fluid 2/2 by the institution's single-deepest-pocket criterion; total 8/8.
Placenta posterior, no previa.
reports.conclusion: Single live cephalic fetus with markedly reduced amniotic fluid (AFI 3 cm). Biophysical profile normal, 8/8.

documents.title: Obstetric Triage and Admission H&P
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Date of service: 05/01/2025 09:10

28 y/o G1P0 at 35w2d by LMP consistent with first-trimester ultrasound, presenting with clear fluid leaking intermittently from the vagina since about 03:00, roughly 6 hours. No contractions. No vaginal bleeding. Fetal movement normal. Prenatal course has been uncomplicated with adequate care and normal growth scans.

PMH: generalized anxiety disorder, hypothyroidism, iron deficiency anemia.
PSH: laparoscopic appendectomy age 16; wisdom teeth extraction.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg daily, sertraline 50 mg daily, prenatal vitamin with iron daily, docusate 100 mg PRN.
Allergies: PENICILLIN (anaphylaxis); LATEX (contact dermatitis).
FH: mother with PPROM; father with type 2 diabetes; sister with chorioamnionitis in a prior pregnancy.
SH: marketing coordinator, never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: VS stable, afebrile. Abdomen gravid, uterus soft and non-tender, fundal height appropriate for dates. Sterile speculum: clear fluid pooling in the posterior vault. Nitrazine positive. Ferning seen on microscopy. Cervix not examined digitally.
Ultrasound: cephalic, AFI 3 cm, BPP 8/8.

A/P: PPROM at 35w2d.
- Admit to L&D. Given >=34 wk, plan delivery; induction with oxytocin.
- GBS status unknown. Severe penicillin allergy (anaphylaxis): vancomycin 1 g IV q12h for GBS prophylaxis.
- Continuous fetal monitoring. Monitor for signs of infection.
- Continue home levothyroxine, sertraline, PNV.
- Latex precautions.

documents.title: Obstetrics Event Note — Intrapartum Fever
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Date of service: 05/01/2025 21:00

Called for maternal fever. Membranes ruptured about 18 hours ago. Since about 15:00 she has had lower abdominal pain and felt feverish; now 6 hours of symptoms. On oxytocin.

T 38.7 C (101.7 F), HR 110, BP 120/75.
FHR baseline 170 bpm.
Uterus tender to palpation, worst at the fundus.

Labs: WBC 18.0, Hgb 12.2, Plt 250. CRP 24 mg/L (ref <10). UA unremarkable.

Impression: intra-amniotic infection (chorioamnionitis) in the setting of PPROM.
Plan:
- Continue vancomycin; add gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV daily (penicillin anaphylaxis precludes ampicillin).
- Acetaminophen 1 g PO for fever.
- Continue oxytocin, anticipate vaginal delivery.
- Newborn team to attend delivery.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admission: 05/01/2025   Discharge: 05/04/2025

Admitting diagnosis: preterm premature rupture of membranes at 35 weeks 2 days.
Additional diagnosis: intra-amniotic infection (chorioamnionitis).

Hospital course: Admitted from triage after rupture was confirmed by pooling, nitrazine and ferning, with an AFI of 3 cm and a BPP of 8/8. GBS status was unknown, so she received vancomycin for prophylaxis given her penicillin anaphylaxis, and oxytocin induction was started. That evening she developed fever to 38.7 with maternal and fetal tachycardia, fundal tenderness and a WBC of 18.0, consistent with intra-amniotic infection. Gentamicin was added. She progressed and had a spontaneous vaginal delivery on 05/02/2025 at 04:40 at 35 weeks 3 days. Liveborn infant, received by the newborn team; infant care is documented separately in the newborn record.

Antibiotics were discontinued after delivery. She remained afebrile postpartum with a firm, non-tender fundus and normal lochia. Ambulating, voiding, tolerating diet.

Discharge medications: levothyroxine 88 mcg daily; sertraline 50 mg daily; prenatal vitamin with iron daily; docusate 100 mg as needed.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis); latex.

Obstetric history now G1P0101.

Follow-up: obstetrics postpartum visit in 6 weeks; primary care within 2 weeks. Return for fever, heavy bleeding, foul discharge, worsening abdominal pain, or mood concerns.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Phone Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 2 days after discharge (delivered 5/2 at 35 wks after PPROM, treated for chorio). Discharge summary received and in chart. Pt says she is sore and tired but ok. No fever since the hospital, bleeding like a heavy period and slowing down, no clots bigger than a quarter, no calf swelling. Taking levothyroxine, sertraline, prenatal. Mood "up and down, mostly ok." Reviewed warning signs: fever, soaking a pad an hour, foul discharge, chest pain, thoughts of harming self - call or go in. Appt made with PCP 5/14.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Admitted 5/1 at 35w2d with PPROM (AFI 3, BPP 8/8), got vanc for GBS ppx because of her PCN anaphylaxis, induced. Developed intra-amniotic infection that evening - T 38.7, HR 110, fetal tachycardia 170, fundal tenderness, WBC 18, CRP 24. Gent added. SVD 5/2, antibiotics stopped after. Home 5/4. Discharge summary reviewed, med rec done - no new meds, no changes.

Today she is 12 days postpartum. No fevers. Bleeding much lighter. Some perineal soreness, improving. Eating and sleeping when she can. Bowels ok, using docusate. Mood: tearful a couple of times the first week, better now. Anxious about getting back to normal but no hopelessness, no thoughts of self-harm. Taking sertraline daily.
GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 5.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Tired-appearing but well. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, non-tender, fundus not palpable above the pubis. Calves soft, non-tender. Affect appropriate, a little tired.

A/P:
1. Postpartum after PPROM and chorioamnionitis, treated - recovering as expected. OB postpartum visit is in June.
2. GAD - stable, continue sertraline 50. Will keep an eye on postpartum mood; she knows to call.
3. Hypothyroidism - TSH today, continue 88 mcg.
4. IDA - CBC and ferritin today. Continue prenatal with iron.
5. Records - discharge summary scanned.

documents.title: Lab results from your visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Iris - thyroid is normal, stay on the 88 mcg. Hemoglobin is 11.4 and ferritin 13, both a little lower than in August, which is expected after delivery. Please keep taking the prenatal vitamin with iron every day. We'll recheck at your physical later this summer. Hope you're getting some rest.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you! Will do.

documents.title: Obstetrics Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Postpartum visit 06/12/2025, 6 weeks after preterm vaginal delivery complicated by PPROM and intra-amniotic infection.

Recovering well. Lochia has stopped. No fever, pelvic pain or urinary symptoms. Mood reported as stable on sertraline.
Exam: BP normal. Abdomen soft, non-tender. Perineum healed. Uterus normal size, non-tender. 

Assessment: normal postpartum recovery. Discussed that PPROM and chorioamnionitis may recur in a future pregnancy and that she should come to us early when pregnant.
Meds unchanged: levothyroxine 88 mcg, sertraline 50 mg, prenatal vitamin with iron, docusate PRN. Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), latex.
Return to primary care for ongoing care.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Turns 29 tomorrow. About 3.5 months out from her May delivery and feeling much more like herself. Back at work. Sleeping better. Anxiety well controlled on sertraline 50 - GAD-7 4, PHQ-9 2. Takes levothyroxine 88 mcg every morning. Still on the prenatal with iron daily; docusate rarely.

ROS otherwise negative: no fatigue beyond the usual, no palpitations, no menstrual concerns, no bowel or urinary issues, no rashes.

PMH: GAD, hypothyroidism, IDA. OB: G1P0101 - PPROM 35 wks 5/2025 with chorioamnionitis, SVD.
PSH: lap appy at 16, wisdom teeth.
Allergies: PCN (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).
FH: mother PPROM, father T2DM, sister chorioamnionitis.
SH: marketing coordinator; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted. NAD. HEENT normal. Thyroid normal size, no nodules. No adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rashes. Extremities without edema. Neuro grossly normal. Mood and affect normal. Pelvic deferred - Pap not due until 2026.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: Pap 6/2023 NILM, next due 2026. HIV/hep B/hep C screened negative with prenatal labs. Flu and COVID in the fall. Tdap given 3/2025.
2. GAD - doing well, continue sertraline 50.
3. Hypothyroidism - TSH today.
4. IDA - CBC, ferritin. Continue prenatal with iron.
Follow up in 6 months or sooner.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Iris, good news on your labs. Hemoglobin is back to 12.1 (normal) and ferritin is up to 21. Thyroid normal on 88 mcg. No changes - keep doing what you're doing. Happy belated birthday!

documents.title: Delivery Note
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Date of service: 05/03/2026

29 y/o G2P0101 at 39w0d (EDD 05/10/2026) admitted in spontaneous labor at 02:40. Prenatal care began early and this pregnancy has been uncomplicated. History of PPROM with intra-amniotic infection at 35 weeks in 2025. Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), latex - latex-free room.

Spontaneous vaginal delivery at 08:12 of a full-term male infant. Amniotic fluid clear.

Newborn: good tone and a strong cry at birth. Cord clamped and cut; infant placed on mother's abdomen. Pink initially, then mild central cyanosis by the end of the first minute. HR 140, RR 50 with good respiratory effort, active muscle tone, crying vigorously. Warm room; infant dried and stimulated with back rubbing. Cyanosis resolved with routine care by 5 minutes. Term infant to routine newborn care with the pediatric team.

Placenta delivered spontaneously, intact. EBL within normal limits. Mother stable.
